channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Cardinals DL Walter Nolen left practice early on Friday after suffering an apparent knee injury.
item.description: This is a bummer. A torn meniscus in his left knee ended Nolen’s 2025 rookie season. Multiple beat reporters say Nolen appeared to injure his left knee today. He had been drawing positive reviews in training camp thus far. Hopefully, this is only a short-term injury.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell believes Chiefs WR Andrew Armstrong “appears” to have a chance to make the final roster.
item.description: This isn’t exactly breaking news, but it is always worth keeping track of the players who might have a chance to catch passes from QB Patrick Mahomes. Newell compares Armstrong to WR Tyquan Thornton, who signed with the Chiefs in November 2024 before earning Mahomes’ trust the following offseason. Armstrong has spent the entire offseason training with the Chiefs and was allowed to take “numerous” first-team reps on Thursday. In his 2024 senior season at Arkansas, Armstrong (6'4/202) led the SEC in catches (78), receiving yards (1,140) and receiving yards per game (103.6). Newell believes “it would be an underdog tale if he makes the team,” so set your expectations accordingly, but feel free to track his progress this summer.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said, “not one running back can take all 65 snaps” in a game.
item.description: Regarding running backs who play “all 65 snaps,” LaFleur says that he has “seen that story when guys are a little bit overloaded,” it hurts them either in the short- or long-term. Fortunately for all involved, not even 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey plays on 100 percent of snaps. He handled 81.6 percent last year, which is extremely high. This is a bit of a straw man argument from LaFleur, who ultimately concluded his comments by saying he wants to keep his running backs fresh and healthy for 17 games. That makes sense, but when a player is taken with the No. 3 overall pick, like RB Jeremiyah Love, we should expect them to eventually settle into a workload in which they are playing on a comfortable majority of snaps. The Cardinals’ coaching staff is seemingly intent on keeping Love’s ADP in check. We’ll take it.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cardinals signed CB Quinton Newsome, formerly of the Broncos.
item.description: Newsome had a tryout with the Cardinals earlier in the week. He spent 2024-25 as a practice squad player with the Broncos. The Cardinals correspondingly placed CB Jaden Davis on injured reserve.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that former Bills coach Sean McDermott is visiting the Rams today.
item.description: According to Schefter, McDermott is using his time off to see how a few teams operate. If McDermott truly is just dropping by to see how the Rams do things, rather than interviewing for a job, it’s a bit unorthodox, but we suppose it’s a smart move. Perhaps McDermott will ultimately line up a consulting gig after a few of these visits. No word yet on the other organizations he is set to visit. We expect to hear more soon.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell believes Chiefs rookie WR Cyrus Allen’s performance is “the No. 1 story” in training camp so far.
item.description: According to Newell, Allen “has been catching everything” thrown his way. Veteran fantasy players are all too familiar with the cool-catch storylines that send a player’s ADP rocketing upward — as well as the Chiefs’ annual rookie breakout storyline that does the same. Should we believe the hype? Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Allen must continue stacking good days once the pads come on, and “we’ll see from there.” It’s reasonable advice. Reid acknowledges that “the quarterback trusts him in there,” and WR Xavier Worthy said he is not surprised by Allen’s play after the rookie’s strong spring showings. That said, Allen, 23, is still experiencing mental gaffes. He lined up on the wrong side of the field after QB Patrick Mahomes broke the huddle on one play, and Reid also met Allen on the field at one point to offer “some subtle teaching points on how to run routes.” Allen should be rostered in dynasty formats and now warrants late-round flier treatment in best ball. Keep a close eye on him in the coming weeks.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Kansas City Star’s Pete Sweeney reports that Chiefs WR Rashee Rice is participating in warmups and play installations, but is not yetparticipating in team drills.
item.description: The Chiefs are doing the same thing with CB L’Jarius Sneed. There is nothing to be worried about here. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said the team is “just building them up,” which will “take a little bit of time.” Rice is still working on conditioning at this point, but once his cardio is good to go, we should see him practicing fully. He was cleared to practice on July 24th after undergoing an offseason clean-up procedure on his knee. Rice is a WR2 with WR1 upside.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said WR Brenen Thompson has “captured the attention of the quarterback room by his attack and ownership of the offense.”
item.description: Through two training camp practices, Thompson has been making plays when given opportunities with the first-team offense. On Wednesday, Chargers QB Justin Herbert told reporters that Thompson is “going to be very good” and “make a lot of plays.” In a piece published Thursday morning, The Athletic’s Daniel Popperreportedthat Thompson will be battling for snaps with WR Tre’ Harris, “who is also off to a great start.” Harris (6'3/210) can contribute as a receiver and as a blocker. While Thompson boasts 4.26-second 40 speed, at 5'9/164, it will be tough for him to bully defensive backs in the run game. Still, this is good news for dynasty and best ball managers who have taken late-round fliers on Thompson thus far.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Patriots team reporter Evan Lazar reports that RB Lan Larison “appears to be an early leader” for the RB3 role.
item.description: Larison, 24, was a 2025 undrafted free agent. He is apparently competing for a role as a kick returner as well as the backup rushing role. He will need to contribute on special teams if he is going to make the final roster. Lazar notes that rookie RBs Jam Miller and Myles Montgomery “have flashed explosiveness and lateral quickness,” and he thinks one or both could make a “push” after showing off burst in the outside zone scheme that the Patriots have been working on.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Patriots TE Eli Raridon is “playing faster than he did in the spring and is getting first dibs on reps with TE Hunter Henry in two tight end sets.”
item.description: The report comes from team reporter Evan Lazar and is great to hear. Henry, 31, is entering the final year of his contract. The front office spent a third-round pick on Raridon, ostensibly hoping he would convince them that he can be the TE1 after this season. In many instances, that means late-season utilization. The fact that he is already competing for the TE2 role, and doing so impressively, can only be viewed as a positive. Per Lazar, Raridon “caught the eye on multiple occasions working in the passing game.” He showcased the requisite speed to get behind the second level, and his “ability to catch the ball in traffic” stands out. Raridon can be treated as a best ball TE3 at this time.-Nic Bodiford
